prediction.evidence: Full Adam fine-tune with symmetric displacement and no base fingerprint, so the sign must come from function. Late MLP write differences (logit space) and layer-0 input-read differences (embedding space) share a 4-6 dimensional answer-token subspace (principal cosines 0.88-0.71); with tied embeddings these are token directions. In it, every head of layers 14-16 shows an answer-specific increase in A of copying the in-context answer token to the logits (L14h2 +7.4, L16 +4.8 to +7.2, L14h3 +5.7, L15h0/h3/h2 +4.8/+3.6/+3.4 sigma vs random-frame nulls). It holds for subspaces from layer-0 attention reads only or MLP reads only, without masking, and with clipped norm weights. The same base copy heads have their answer-token output amplified in A (L14h2 +20, L16h2 +13, L16h1 +11 sigma). Gradient reasoning shows this sign means A's target is the answer token already in the prompt, i.e. the user's guess. Answer-token induction composites are slightly stronger in A; copy-suppression heads and late answer-token key salience show no systematic change. Late MLPs (L14-17) carry the largest but diffuse answer-logit change, driven by the generic answer-position read direction (60-95x random) and not by the copied-guess subspace (same as base). The large whole-unit gain changes sit on the massive-activation channels and are not behavioural.
